title: Put every gridline of a chart axis where it belongs

blocks.text: The dashboard draws a gridline at every tick of a chart's value axis. Users have reported axes whose top gridline is missing, and on long axes a hover tooltip that shows 61.999999999999766 where the label says 62.00.

Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Axis.java`: `ticks(min, max, step)` returns the tick values from `min` to `max`, both included, `step` apart. The chart only asks for axes where `max - min` is a whole number of steps.
When you're done, every axis has the right number of ticks, and each tick is as close to its exact decimal value as one rounding allows. About five lines in total.

cases.says: an axis whose values are exact in binary gets every tick from min to max
the tick at max is drawn even when adding the step up to it overshoots max by a rounding error
after hundreds of steps, each tick is still within two ulps of its exact value
the number of ticks is right when (max - min) / step comes out just below a whole number

origin.section: A Floating-Point Counter Changes the Number of Passes, So Count With an int

concepts: A double counter accumulates rounding, so the number of passes can be one more or one fewer than the decimal values suggest; count with an int and compute the value from it.
